quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What do speed limit signs show?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area
The highest or lowest speed allowed by law
The speed to drive in heavy traffic
The speed to drive in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest speed allowed by law
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the highest or lowest safe speed allowed on a road. The maximum speed is for perfect conditions. You must slow down when conditions are worse.

questions.question: If you park in an unusual spot:

options.text: Leave your reverse lights on.
Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your parked car is not a hazard. No matter where you park, other drivers must be able to see your vehicle from all directions.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
Check the inside rearview mirror.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see if the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: You may carefully continue through a yellow light if:

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
Pedestrians are crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when a yellow light appears, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: After being pulled over, a driver should immediately exit the vehicle and quickly approach the officer's car.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: When stopped by law enforcement, stay in your vehicle with both hands visible on the steering wheel.

questions.question: To make a right turn correctly:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the center before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner from the right lane, but move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, use your signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay in the right lane as close as possible to the right curb or edge of the road.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:

options.text: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
Keep the same speed.
Stay in the blind spot.
Honk to alert the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or backward so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Never drive in someone's blind spot. Move forward or backward so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
If there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signal.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, check:

options.text: The inside rearview mirror.
The outside rearview mirror.
Over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots cannot be seen in your mirrors. Look over your shoulders to check your blind spots.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
There is no need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Large vehicles have blind spots that extend up to 200 feet behind them.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have blind spots up to 200 feet behind them. Do not tailgate large vehicles because the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They use vibration and noise to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use vibration and noise to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes you to make errors with speed and distance judgment. It slows down your decision-making and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel, which can injure or kill you and others.

questions.question: What does this yellow warning sign mean?

options.text: You are approaching a school or school crosswalk.
Slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed near schools to warn drivers to slow down, drive carefully, and watch for children.

questions.question: Which traffic light tells you to slow down and proceed with caution?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, proceed carefully, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane, two-way road, you must cross into the oncoming traffic lane to pass safely. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a railroad crossing sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going further.
Slow down and yield for trains.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead. Always slow down at railroad crossings. Trains cannot move out of your way, so you must let them pass first.

questions.question: As your speed increases, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer stopping distances. When driving fast, look ahead to give yourself time to safely react to hazards.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either direction.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. Passing is not allowed from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if it is on a private road.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and a stop arm out. This rule applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
May drive through if the road is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You may also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcycles a full lane width. They need room to maneuver safely, even if there seems to be enough space to share the lane.

questions.question: When a driver is tailgating you:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If there is no right lane, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed to let them pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slowly reduce speed to encourage them to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of a rear-end crash.

questions.question: You may park or stop on a freeway shoulder:

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a curve or hill because fewer vehicles are coming.
By driving on the highway shoulder.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Never pass across a solid yellow line.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest choice is to:

options.text: Change your speed frequently to stay alert.
Drive faster than the flow of traffic.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand danger and might run into the street without looking.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence when a school bus prepares to stop for children?

options.text: Amber lights flash, the bus stops with red lights flashing, the stop arm comes out, and the door opens for children.
The bus turns on red flashing lights, then turns on amber flashing lights after children are unloaded or seated.
The stop arm comes out, amber lights flash, and the bus stops to load or unload children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Amber lights flash, the bus stops with red lights flashing, the stop arm comes out, and the door opens for children.
questions.explanation: When you see amber flashing lights on a school bus, slow to 20 mph or less and be ready to stop. When red lights flash or the stop arm is out, stop at least 15 feet away. Stay stopped while the red lights flash or the stop arm is out.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you can pass another vehicle from either direction.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle can cross the centerline to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Prevents distractions from other vehicles.
Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
Keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Do not brake immediately.
Slowly reduce speed and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Remove your foot from the gas and do not brake right away. Slowly reduce speed, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop and let pedestrians and other traffic pass.
Stop and drive immediately.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let pedestrians and other traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at the marked line before the crosswalk or intersection. Let other vehicles and pedestrians pass if they are in your path, then go.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk straight after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your judgment. You need good judgment to react safely while driving. Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.
